thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple nodes in inference-pool showing NotReady / kubelet restarts. Auto-escalation to oncall.

Maya (oncall): seeing a spike in 5xx and timeouts for the small-model route, started ~10m ago. dashboards -> inference-pool eu-west.

Ryan (runtime): logs show repeated container restarts with OOMs and some CUDA failures: `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT` in the worker pods on gke-infer-12/gke-infer-14.

Maya (oncall): pinging @Tom for node-level, @Sasha for routing fallback. Is this still contained to two nodes?

Tom (infra): I can confirm gke-infer-12 went NotReady at ~1912345600, kubelet restarted twice. Nodes gke-infer-14 flapped a couple of times. Kube events: `kubelet: frequent heartbeat loss`.

infra-bot: node gke-infer-12: status -> NotReady (KubeletRestart), restartCount=3. Scheduling impacted: 22 pods evicted/failed to schedule.

Ryan (runtime): stack traces include repeated CUDA launch failures during multi-batch decoding; then the container hits memory limit and OOMs. Might be driver/firmware mismatch after kernel update? Not seeing kernel upgrades in node history though.

Maya (oncall): customer impact: a handful of customers behind low-traffic API keys reported elevated latency and 502s. No major SLA breach yet but error budget trending up.

Sasha (platform): I'm flipping routing to avoid that AZ's inference pool and enabling model-variant fallback (smaller quantized variant) for the small-model route. Will post when roll completes.

Tom (infra): immediate mitigation plan: cordon gke-infer-12, drain non-critical inference pods, force-restart kubelet if it doesn't stabilize, and spin up two replacement nodes from the dedicated pool to rebalance.

Maya (oncall): executing manual failover now: scaling small-model horizontal target from 30->45, and enabling rapid fallback to dedicated capacity.

Ryan (runtime): also pushing a hotfix to reduce batch size for that model route and disable a new dynamic-prefetch flag that seems to exacerbate memory growth. Command I ran in staging: 
```
kubectl -n production set env deploy/small-model BATCH_MAX_SIZE=4 PREFETCH=false
```

Maya (oncall): noted. rolling patch to prod now; will monitor error rate.

infra-bot: New nodes gke-infer-21 and gke-infer-22 provisioned and joined cluster.

Tom (infra): kubelet logs from gke-infer-12 attached: `E0814 12:34:50 kubelet.go:234] runtime network failed: dial tcp: connection refused` then `kubelet: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address`. I'm scheduling a kernel reboot if kubelet doesn't recover.

Ryan (runtime): observed one pod on gke-infer-14 with `containerLogs: /var/log/containers/worker-*.log` showing repeated `cuLaunchKernel failed: 700` then sudden `OOMKilled`. Suggest we temporarily taint nodes with `no-infer=true:NoSchedule` while we investigate driver state.

Maya (oncall): applying taint to the two flappy nodes now to prevent rescheduling.

Sasha (platform): fallback routing complete. Traffic to smaller quantized variant at 100% for the affected route. Latency is back to baseline for most customers. Monitoring shows errors decreased by 78%. :thumbsup:

Tom (infra): kubelet on gke-infer-12 recovered after a restart but I'm leaving it cordoned until we run a node repro and driver checks. Will collect `dmesg` and nvdriver logs.

Ryan (runtime): keeping the smaller batch size config for next 6 hours, then we can ramp back if stable. I'll also add an eval to detect memory growth spikes during decode.

Maya (oncall): preparing short incident summary for pager duty and CS: impact, mitigation steps, nodes affected, follow-up (drivers, kernel, tesla driver validation). Taking handoff in 30m: @Tom, you'll own node remediation and logs; @Ryan you'll own runtime config revert plan and postmortem evals.

Tom (infra): acknowledged, will collect logs, `kubectl describe node` outputs, `journalctl` and nvdriver outputs and create a ticket with attachments.

Ryan (runtime): acknowledged. I'll add a perf/regression alert to catch batch-size-induced memory spikes and add a canary for PREFETCH=false.

Maya (oncall): handing off - I'm logging this incident in incidents/ with tag `node-flap-inference-failover`. If anything devolves, re-ping @Maya and I'll rejoin.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigation-in-progress. Handed off to Tom (infra) & Ryan (runtime).

Sasha (platform): brief note for CS: "We observed transient node instability in one region impacting inference latency for a subset of requests. Traffic has been shifted to a smaller model variant and dedicated capacity while the nodes are remediated. No data loss. Engineering is investigating drivers and kubelet restarts."

Maya (oncall): closing thread for now, will update when postmortem draft is ready. Thanks all.
